title: cell-workspace-v1 documents
description: Machine-readable contract for the cell workspace documents of spec/cell-workspaces-v1.md: a Request, a Record and a Result, each self-identified by schema cell-workspace/v1. The schema is DESCRIPTIVE of shape: required fields, field types, patterns and closed value sets. It does NOT encode the cross-field rules the workspace module enforces (task-or-session by kind, detached subjects for review/verify/check, lease on active, git identity past allocating, repo_key derived from repo, payload digest equality on replay, the transition table, an outcome's reason matching its kind); where the two disagree the schema is the LOOSER on purpose. Keys match exactly, case included; a decoder refuses a repeated key, a null or empty optional field and trailing data.

Operation.description: Version 1 defines allocation only. Later lifecycle operations join this set under the same envelope; a reader refuses an operation it does not know with unsupported-capability.

Kind.description: What the workspace is for. Path and branch are attributes, never identity.

State.description: Lifecycle state. Refusal, conflict and unknown evidence are outcomes, never states.

Reason.description: refused: unknown-schema, malformed, invalid, unsupported-capability, payload-mismatch, identity-mismatch, illegal-transition. conflict: stale-generation, foreign-state. unknown: busy, evidence-unavailable.

CellRef.description: The admitted cell: its durable UUID and the root it is admitted at.

root.description: At most 4096 bytes in decoded UTF-8, including the root; the Go validator is authoritative. maxLength counts characters and is only a necessary ceiling (spec section 3).

RepoRef.description: Canonical repository identity: forge instance and repository path. Never a URL, user or credential.

SessionRef.description: The role session the request runs under.

Ref.description: A reference into an existing owner; the workspace record is never a second store for it.

Subject.description: The exact commit the checkout holds, pinned before any checkout exists. review, verify and check workspaces are detached; branch mode names its branch.

Path.description: Platform-native logical path and the resolved physical path the effect boundary verified. Every path in these documents (here, cell.root and the Git directories) is an absolute local path: a POSIX root or a drive root, never a network root, a .. segment or a control character (spec section 3).

logical.description: At most 4096 bytes in decoded UTF-8, including the root; the Go validator is authoritative. maxLength counts characters and is only a necessary ceiling (spec section 3).

physical.description: At most 4096 bytes in decoded UTF-8, including the root; the Go validator is authoritative. maxLength counts characters and is only a necessary ceiling (spec section 3).

GitIdentity.description: Git administration identity verified at effect time.

common_dir.description: At most 4096 bytes in decoded UTF-8, including the root; the Go validator is authoritative. maxLength counts characters and is only a necessary ceiling (spec section 3).

admin_dir.description: At most 4096 bytes in decoded UTF-8, including the root; the Go validator is authoritative. maxLength counts characters and is only a necessary ceiling (spec section 3).

Outcome.description: Typed answer. An ok outcome carries no reason; every other outcome carries the reason its kind is defined by.

Request.description: One operation request. (cell, repository, kind, task-or-session, attempt_id, request_id) is the idempotency key; the payload digest binds the rest. A desk request names its session and no task; every other kind names its task or claim.

require.description: Capabilities the serving implementation must declare; an undeclared one is refused, never downgraded.

Record.description: The durable state of one workspace. generation increases by one on every transition and is the compare-and-set token; a record past allocating carries its verified git identity; an active record carries a process lease; a retained record names its reason; a legacy record is never allocating or ready.

Result.description: The answer to a request. Only an ok result carries a record, so no failure hands a caller a path.

$comment: Paths are limited to 4096 decoded UTF-8 bytes by the authoritative Go validator (spec section 3). JSON Schema maxLength counts characters and is only a necessary ceiling, not the byte check. Wire UTF-8 and surrogate-pair integrity must be checked before a JSON parser can replace malformed input.
